bullets.title: Apple Intelligence approved in China via Alibaba Qwen integration — BABA +5% premarket
bullets.body: China has approved Apple's on-device AI model, with Alibaba's Qwen AI to be integrated into Apple Intelligence across iOS, iPadOS, macOS, and visionOS in China. US-listed Alibaba shares rose 5% premarket on the report, reflecting the AI partnership's strategic significance for both companies.

bullets.title: Morgan Stanley Q2 equities trading crushes at $6.30B vs. $4.47B estimate
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley reported Q2 2026 total revenue of $21.35B vs. $19.58B estimate, with equities sales & trading revenue of $6.30B nearly 41% above the $4.47B consensus. Wealth management net revenue of $8.86B also beat estimates, while FICC at $2.46B was a slight miss vs. $2.56B expected.

bullets.title: US-Iran military strikes: CENTCOM targets Hormuz shipping corridor; crude ~$80/bbl
bullets.body: US Central Command launched strikes against Iran beginning 6am ET, completing morning operations by 7:30am ET, with the stated aim of degrading Iran's ability to attack commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. Iran's IRGC threatened to halt all oil and gas exports from the region if the US maintains presence; WTI and Brent crude trading around $80/barrel.

bullets.title: PayPal receives reported $53–60.50/share buyout bid from Stripe and Advent; SEC probes pre-deal call surge
bullets.body: PayPal reportedly received an acquisition offer from privately-held Stripe and Advent at $60.50/share per WSJ. Call volume surged ahead of the deal report and has been flagged to the SEC, suggesting potential pre-announcement information leakage.

bullets.title: Buffett confirms he personally initiated Berkshire's Google investment, says he made a mistake not buying earlier
bullets.body: Warren Buffett told CNBC he was the one who initiated Berkshire Hathaway's investment in Alphabet and admitted he made a mistake not buying Google stock earlier. The disclosure signals conviction-level bullishness from Berkshire on GOOGL.

bullets.title: NVDA, AVGO, MU, GOOGL cited as leading market recovery intraday
bullets.body: One fintwit account noted that NVDA, AVGO, MU, and GOOGL are 'trying to save the markets,' pointing to large-cap tech as the primary driver of intraday bid. Jensen Huang's ongoing Asia tour — now in Japan — is expected to generate additional NVDA/Japanese company headlines this week.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler credit stress hits all-time high as data-center debt boom draws scrutiny
bullets.body: Bloomberg flagged that signs of hyperscaler credit stress have reached the highest levels since Goldman Sachs launched its basket in February, as the data-center building boom has sparked an explosion of debt funding. One commentator noted investors are not paying adequate attention to lending terms.

bullets.title: Softer PPI follows CPI miss; macro backdrop supports equities, rates steady
bullets.body: Headline PPI came in at 0% MoM (prior 1.1%) and core PPI at 0.3% MoM (prior 0.4%), following yesterday's softer CPI print. The combined data moderated market expectations for Fed rate hikes and provided a boost to stocks; separately, NEC Director Hassett argued the data shows 'no excuse for raising rates' and that Warsh's influence will drive the Fed to the right answer.

bullets.title: BofA fund manager survey: 54% see no recession; most bullish since February
bullets.body: The latest BofA fund manager survey shows 54% of respondents expect a 'no landing' scenario — a record high — with only 2% anticipating a hard landing. Sentiment is the most bullish since February, and 83% of respondents expect no Fed rate hikes before the midterms.

bullets.title: China Q2 GDP slows to 4.3%, weakest in decades ex-Covid; chip exports only bright spot
bullets.body: China's annual growth decelerated from 5% in Q1 to 4.3% in Q2, below consensus and the lowest in decades outside of Covid. One macro commentator argued that without chip export support, China's overall economy would likely be contracting, with deleveraging malaise worsening.

bullets.title: June CPI detail: core goods +0.8% YoY, core services +3.2% YoY; real wages turn positive
bullets.body: Both core goods and core services inflation showed notable easing in June, with core goods at +0.8% YoY and core services at +3.2% YoY. Inflation-adjusted average hourly and weekly earnings turned positive YoY in June after two consecutive monthly declines, aided by easing gas prices.

bullets.title: NFIB small business: labor quality concerns spike — largest monthly jump since 1985
bullets.body: The percentage of small businesses citing labor quality as their top issue jumped 6 percentage points in June, the third-largest month-over-month increase since 1985. Capital spending plans rose to their highest reading of the year, while overall labor metrics remain in multiyear downtrends.

bullets.title: Citigroup cuts Microsoft price target to $570 from $620
bullets.body: Citigroup reduced its Microsoft price target by $50 (8.1% downward revision) to $570 from $620, signaling reduced near-term conviction on MSFT.

bullets.title: IBM rally since May called 'one of the most absurd episodes' in current asset bubble
bullets.body: A fintwit commentator characterized IBM's stock rally since May as 'one of the most absurd episodes' in the current asset bubble environment, suggesting market pricing mechanisms are broken following IBM's unexpected Tuesday update.

bullets.title: Intel 18A Panther Lake chips leveraging ASML High-NA EUV for production
bullets.body: Intel is using ASML's High-NA EUV technology to produce its 18A Panther Lake chips, a positive signal for Intel's advanced manufacturing roadmap execution.

bullets.title: Photonics sector showing signs of bottoming; LITE strongest, AXTI and AAOI stabilizing
bullets.body: One tech-focused fintwit account flagged that photonics stocks are 'trying to find a low,' with AXTI attempting to reverse after a three-month downtrend and AAOI also stabilizing. LITE is called out as the strongest name in the sector.

bullets.title: Reddit contrarian bull: 'RDDT is printing cash' despite 'dead' narrative
bullets.body: One fintwit account pushed back against bearish Reddit sentiment, stating flatly that 'Reddit is printing cash' and characterizing the 'RDDT is dead' narrative as incorrect.

bullets.title: White House not ruling out regulatory action on open-source AI models
bullets.body: Semafor reports the White House is not ruling out action on open-source AI models, adding a potential regulatory overhang to the open-source AI ecosystem.

bullets.title: NY Governor Hochul's datacenter moratorium framed as temporary framework-setting pause
bullets.body: Governor Hochul's one-year pause on new datacenter approvals in New York is being characterized as a temporary measure to establish better agreement structures, not a permanent ban. Hochul has stated she supports AI as a driver of future growth and uses AI herself.

bullets.title: Dan Ives departs Wedbush to launch Yorkville Ives merchant bank
bullets.body: Star tech analyst Dan Ives has left Wedbush Securities to form Yorkville Ives, a new merchant bank, removing one of the most prominent bulls on large-cap tech from a major sell-side platform.
